A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRUST/TRUST++ research, despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments on tractable models, likelihood-free benchmarks, and nuisance-parameter problems, including coverage comparisons and confidence-region visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation results and adds detailed per-scenario numerical results in Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: Equation 5 changes the partition empirical CDF from count/m to (count+1)/(m+1), and Algorithms 1–2 now specify adjusted alpha-quantiles. This changes the stated finite-sample cutoff calculation while retaining the tree/forest construction, proximity neighborhoods, tuning, and nuisance-parameter approach.

E1.justification: Both versions use Normal, Gaussian-mixture and lognormal models; SLCP, Two Moons, M/G/1, Weinberg and SIR benchmarks; and Poisson-counting and Gamma-GLM nuisance problems. The descriptions moved into Appendix A.1 retain the same data-generating processes and inference tasks.

E2.justification: Gradient-boosting quantile regression, Monte Carlo, and asymptotic calibration where applicable remain the comparison methods. The TRUST/TRUST++ variants are also retained. The new appendix displays do not introduce another comparator.

E3.justification: v1 Figure 4 includes tractable-model results for n=1,5,10,20,50,100; v2 Section 5.1 and Figure 4 restrict reporting to n=10,20,50,100. Thus n=20 was already evaluated in v1 despite its omission from that version's prose. Simulation budgets, evaluation metrics, and the stated LFI and nuisance-problem settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 Figures 5 and 7 analyze the fraction of scenarios satisfying progressively tighter MAE thresholds and the error distributions within those subsets. These diagnostics are removed from v2. The Two Moons uncertainty illustration and nuisance-parameter case studies remain; the new benchmark heatmaps are detailed results rather than new ablations.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 newly describes highlighted methods as attaining the minimum MAE or lying within two standard errors of it. Section 5 retains the overlapping-95%-confidence-interval criterion and the same 50/30/15 replication counts. This adds statistical selection reporting, but does not establish additional runs or reconcile the two criterion formulations.

E6.justification: Appendix A.4 adds extensive per-model, statistic, sample-size and budget MAEs with standard errors in Figures 8–14. Aggregate win counts also change: in Figure 4, tuned TRUST++ has 12 wins at n=10, B=5000 in v1 and 10 in v2. LFI summary counts are revised as well. These are revised reported results, not evidence of a performance gain; nuisance-problem Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The empirical-CDF definition receives the finite-sample adjustment, and Theorems 2–3 now refer to adjusted quantiles. The formal assumptions, coverage conclusions, and Appendix C proof arguments are otherwise retained. Renumbering Lemma 2 as Lemma 1 does not add a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: TRUST/TRUST++ calibration, finite-sample local and simulation-asymptotic conditional coverage, efficient nuisance handling, and uncertainty about estimated confidence sets. The title change to Conformal Calibration does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly clarifies that local coverage depends on the reference distribution r(theta), whereas conditional coverage does not. The expanded results discussion also qualifies applicability more specifically, acknowledging strong asymptotic performance for Normal-model likelihood ratios and a diminishing E-value advantage at larger sample sizes.

D1.justification: The implementation information is retained: scikit-learn tree settings, forest size, tuning algorithm, normalizing-flow architectures and training settings, hardware, and repository disclosure. Model, prior, and statistic descriptions are largely relocated from Sections 5.1–5.2 to Appendix A.1 rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: Section 1.1.3 adds Ding et al. (2023) on class-conditional conformal prediction. The overall positioning relative to conformal prediction, LoCart, and likelihood-free inference remains stable. Updates to the Cabezas and Izbicki references primarily identify published versions of already cited work.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: lengthy model and statistic descriptions move into Appendix A.1, Sections 5.1–5.2 become shorter summaries, and Appendix A.4 introduces detailed result commentary. The title, running headers, captions, and several explanatory passages are also edited.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven numerical heatmap figures, redraws the aggregate comparison plots, removes the two threshold-diagnostic figures, and resizes or relocates retained illustrations. The tractable summary changes from six sample-size columns to four. Appendix result figures now extend through and interrupt the proof material.

improvement.justification: The finite-sample calibration correction and the detailed MAE/standard-error displays make the method and empirical evidence more checkable. The discussion also better identifies settings where competing methods perform well. These gains outweigh the loss of the smallest-sample tractable results and threshold diagnostics, although those removals and the interrupted appendix layout limit the overall improvement.
